summary: A bounded, source-backed production-readiness review of the autonomous assistant itself.

goal.title: Produce a source-backed autonomous production-readiness review
goal.description: Use recent run evidence and the current repository to identify concrete reliability, budget, authorization, recovery, review-loop, and operator-control improvements without changing production.

roadmap_items.title: Establish the recent autonomous-run evidence baseline
roadmap_items.description: Analyze the allowlisted snapshot of up to five recent autonomous runs and produce a concise operational baseline. Use only supplied evidence; do not infer omitted task narratives.
acceptance_criteria: Account for every supplied run using run ID, trigger, final status, and whether human review was required; explicitly state when fewer than five runs were supplied and that per-run cost is unavailable unless supplied.
Keep global run metadata separate from Tyler AI Assistant project details and label unknown information rather than inferring it.
Identify no more than three recurring operational patterns and give one evidence-based next action for each.
Expose no secrets, private narratives, or report paths, and perform no external action.

roadmap_items.title: Audit budget reservations, routing, and reconciliation
roadmap_items.description: Inspect the current budget ledger, model router, autonomous adapter, and their tests. Trace cost control from estimate through reservation and reconciliation. Propose hardening only; do not modify code.
acceptance_criteria: Trace estimate, reservation, affordable-output enforcement, provider usage, reconciliation, and budget-day rollover with source-file plus function or test-name evidence.
Cover success, provider failure, cancellation or timeout, and competing reservations, distinguishing code-proven behavior from live behavior that remains unverified.
List at most five material gaps, each with failure impact and the smallest practical mitigation or test.
Read only repository evidence; expose no secret values and perform no mutation or external action.

roadmap_items.title: Audit scheduling, locking, persistence, and restart recovery
roadmap_items.description: Inspect the autonomous workflow, its tests, and deployment documentation. Produce a fail-closed recovery assessment without touching Railway or persistent state.
acceptance_criteria: Trace scheduler registration, run locking, scheduled-date idempotency, task claiming, report persistence, and run completion with named source or test evidence.
Document state-path precedence, seed-versus-persistent-state behavior, atomic writes, stale-run recovery, and the shared-filesystem assumption.
Provide a failure matrix for overlap, process restart, stale run, corrupt state, and interrupted write, including the expected safe state for each.
Provide an owner recovery checklist that proposes no deletion, redeploy, or state mutation.

roadmap_items.title: Audit autonomous authorization and external-action gates
roadmap_items.description: Inspect authorization filtering, specialist tool profiles, confirmation gates, and relevant tests. Assess bypass risk without requesting broader permissions.
acceptance_criteria: Produce a source-backed matrix mapping observe, propose, modify_local, and external_action to automatic tools, blocked tools, and required human gates.
Identify remote-mutation-capable tools and direct-helper bypass paths, clearly distinguishing reachable autonomous paths from general architectural risk.
Rank at most five authorization risks by severity and give one narrowly scoped mitigation or test for each.
Do not inspect secret values, grant permissions, create branches, send messages, deploy, or mutate external state.

roadmap_items.title: Audit review-loop termination and Telegram escalation behavior
roadmap_items.description: Inspect Company Mode, autonomous aggregation, Telegram behavior, and related tests. Verify that failed work stops spending and produces an actionable terminal outcome.
acceptance_criteria: Trace acceptance criteria from roadmap item through worker prompt, reviewer verdict, revisions, terminal state, persisted report, and Telegram output using named source or test evidence.
Provide expected outcomes for approval, ordinary revision, repeated feedback, missing access, permission failure, budget exhaustion, timeout, task-local blocker, and blocked-session ideation.
Verify or explicitly flag uncertainty around retry caps, no-progress fingerprints, unrelated-work continuation, creative suppression, redaction, chunking, and the trigger/final/human-review row.
List at most five concrete discrepancies or weak spots with the smallest proposed correction; make no changes.

roadmap_items.title: Create the critical autonomous-workflow test-gap matrix
roadmap_items.description: Inspect existing tests and produce a ranked, implementation-ready test plan. Do not run or edit tests.
acceptance_criteria: Map existing test functions to selection, overlap prevention, budget reservation, reconciliation, review caps, blocker continuation, dry-run safety, and redaction.
Identify exactly six highest-value missing or weak scenarios, each with target test file, setup, mocked boundary, expected assertion, and failure prevented.
Avoid proposing duplicate coverage and rank the six scenarios by production risk.
Do not claim tests were executed and do not create or modify files.

roadmap_items.title: Produce the owner go-or-no-go autonomous operations runbook
roadmap_items.description: Use current repository documentation and tests to create a concise Telegram-first checklist for approving the next scheduled live run. Independently inspect its sources rather than relying on prior roadmap-item output.
acceptance_criteria: Provide a one-page pre-run, during-run, post-run, and escalation checklist suitable for the Telegram owner.
Use only commands confirmed by current documentation and explain the exact intent of each command.
Define explicit go-or-no-go conditions for an active Company project, pending confirmation, absent roadmap work, insufficient budget, recovery-required state, and a needs-human task.
State clearly that $5.00 is a ceiling, $0.25 is reserved, exact spending is not guaranteed, and no deploy, merge, permission expansion, or forced token consumption is authorized.
